correctness.rationale: Cauchy determinant positivity is exact; decreasing integrable kernel Riemann sums plus uniform majorants prove the N^(2-alpha) leading coefficient. The geometric case follows by summing equal gaps. In the supergeometric case absolutely summable offdiagonal entries give trace class, and Laplace uniqueness plus Fredholm theory gives strictly positive determinant. Bessel/frame boundary follows from block coherence and positive Toeplitz symbol.

value.rationale: The normalized Laplace orbit is a canonical diagonal continuous-time dynamical sampling model. Its finite Gram determinant is a natural exact measure of stability/volume loss. The sharp power N^(2-alpha) and nontrivial pi-squared coefficient quantify collapse precisely where the infinite analysis operator ceases to be Bessel, with an exponential determinant phase at criticality and a positive Fredholm limit above; these are intrinsic transitions rather than arbitrary parameter slices.
